concepts.description: Word and Markdown have full read/write support, PDF supports reading, extraction, and basic manipulation, plain text is full read/write, and Rich Text is basic read/write.
Document operations preserve formatting and structural organization where the format supports it.
Documents may be created blank, from predefined templates, or by conversion.
Editing covers text, fonts, styles, colors, alignment, headings, lists, and tables.
Tracked changes, revision history, inline comments, and annotations remain supported.
Document generation supports tables and embedded images.
Analysis extracts text and hierarchy, computes word and page counts and reading time, and searches text or patterns.
Conversions cover Word to PDF, PDF to Word, Markdown to Word or PDF, and every supported format to plain text.
PDF-to-Word conversion uses OCR when needed.
The report shortcut creates a Word document with a title page, table-of-contents placeholder, and section headers.
Important documents are backed up before editing.
Collaborative edits use tracked changes to retain history.
Formatting is verified after conversion.
Documents containing many images may process more slowly.
Complex PDF layouts may not convert perfectly to editable formats.
Macros and embedded objects may not be fully supported.
Documents above 50MB may process more slowly.
Encrypted or password-protected documents cannot be accessed without the password.
Recovery checks path existence, permissions, corruption or unsupported format, then retries conversion with a simpler target.
Template, format-support, and troubleshooting references retain their respective guide roles.
